name: Ouroboros
prompt:
Use case: precise-object-edit / fantasy game token refinement.
Image 1 is the edit target, the current three-color Ouroboros medallion. Preserve the exact overall round token framing, front-facing composition, creature's continuous circular body, large recognizable snake head at upper right, physical tail-in-mouth contact, high-quality engraving, comfortable margin and transparent exterior. Create ONE revised asset.

CHANGE 1 — THE ORDER AROUND THE CYCLE:
The body must run RED → VIOLET → BLUE clockwise from the tail at the upper-right bite.
• From roughly 2 o'clock down the entire right side to 6 o'clock: rich coral-red / red-orange Flare (#FF5A3C).
• From 6 o'clock around the lower-left arc to 10 o'clock: rich saturated Abyss VIOLET (#A832D4), with visible purple surfaces and purple highlights, not blue-magenta shading.
• From 10 o'clock across the upper-left/top arc into the head and jaws at upper right: clear sapphire/cobalt BLUE Continuum (#3D6BFF).
Give all three approximately one third of the body and similar visual prominence. There must be one continuous snake, not three creatures. Transition naturally over short interfaces. No gold or green region.

CHANGE 2 — MATERIALS VISIBLY TRANSFORM:
The RED section visibly emerges as an exuberant FIERY BURST around the tail at the bite, then courses along the right-hand arc: sculptural tongues of scarlet flame, glowing embers and molten red scale surfaces. The fire hugs the continuous snake body and does NOT shoot out into open space.
CRITICAL: keep the solid tapered RED TAIL clearly visible entering the BLUE HEAD'S JAWS. The viewer must immediately read a serpent swallowing its own tail, not a dragon merely breathing fire. The flame can make that junction feel like simultaneous consuming and remaking.
The VIOLET section is a substantial mysterious transition: glossy deep-purple scales dissolving into violet luminous mist only at their edges, coherent and strong enough to remain the same body.
The BLUE section visibly CRYSTALLIZES: replace ordinary smooth blue scales with large angular translucent sapphire crystal plates, sharp faceted planes, refracted cool blue light, and small integrated crystalline ridges. The recognizable serpent head itself becomes beautifully faceted blue crystal while retaining its eye, snout, jaws and bite. This is crystallization within the serpent anatomy, not an added crystal object or ice dragon with horns.

CHANGE 3 — SOMETHING IN THE CENTER:
Place a compact suspended luminous seed-core inside the circle, around one quarter of the inner opening's diameter. A red incandescent heart, a rich violet translucent middle layer, and a few bright blue crystalline outer facets are all distinctly visible, with roughly balanced color presence. This central seed is a small emblem of matter reforming, subtly radiating into the surrounding interior. Leave ample clear breathing room between this small core and the surrounding serpent. Do not make the core a giant galaxy, blue vortex, starburst, hole, extra snake or separate token. The surrounding interior can stay deep and quiet; its middle must now visibly contain the luminous three-color core.

RIM: Follow the same RED → VIOLET → BLUE order with three broad equal metal sectors aligned with the body regions: red right/lower-right, violet lower-left, blue upper arc. Each sector's edge lighting and engraved tracery should be colored locally to match that sector. No all-around cyan outline or blue-dominant framework. Retain the original polished affinity-token craftsmanship and restrained engraving.

No labels, words, letters, numbers or new decorative icons. Do not change to a flat symbol or redesign the frame. Preserve genuine transparency outside the complete circular medallion. Output only the single revised Ouroboros.
changes: Fiery red burst around the continuous tail
Small luminous three-color core at the center
